segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַקּוֹרֵא בְּתוֹרָה — לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְּסוּקִים, וְלֹא יִקְרָא לִמְתוּרְגְּמָן יוֹתֵר מִפָּסוּק אֶחָד.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One who reads from the Torah» in the synagogue «should not read fewer than three verses. And» when it is being translated, «he should not read to the translator more than one verse» at a time, so that the translator will not become confused.

segments.he: וּבַנָּבִיא שְׁלֹשָׁה. הָיוּ שְׁלָשְׁתָּן שָׁלֹשׁ פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת — קוֹרִין אֶחָד אֶחָד.
segments.en: «And with regard to the Prophets,» one may read to the translator «three» verses at a time. With respect to the Torah, an incorrect translation might lead to an error in practice, but this concern does not apply to the Prophets. «If the three» verses «constitute three» separate «paragraphs,» that is to say, if each verse is a paragraph in itself, «one must read» them to the translator «one by one.»

segments.he: מְדַלְּגִין בַּנָּבִיא וְאֵין מְדַלְּגִין בַּתּוֹרָה. וְעַד כַּמָּה הוּא מְדַלֵּג? עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְסוֹק הַמְתוּרְגְּמָן.
segments.en: «One may skip» from one place to another while reading «the Prophets, but one may not skip» from one place to another while reading «the Torah. How far may he skip? As far as» he can, provided that «the translator will not conclude» his translation while the reader is still rolling the scroll to the new location. The reader may not cause the congregation to wait for him after the translator has finished, as that would be disrespectful to the congregation.

moves.cueHe: הקורא בתורה לא יפחות משלשה פסוקים
moves.summary: Torah reader reads at least three verses, one at a time to the translator
in Prophets three verses at a time, unless each is a paragraph
skipping allowed in Prophets not Torah, as long as translator does not finish

positions.claim: no fewer than three verses; one verse at a time to the translator in Torah, three in Prophets; skipping allowed in Prophets only
